### Pareto/NSGA-II browser frontier (local, partial)

`sample-pareto-context` runs the shared native NSGA-II kernel against exact hash-checked RCTX. The workbench retains a visible canonical u64 seed, plan-population and generation budgets, tolerance and optional Democratic/minority share arrays in exact unit order. Its tables distinguish unavailable objectives and separately measured final balance/contiguity. Exact native NDJSON downloads retain all frontier candidates, including constraint failures.

The kernel now uses protocol `2.0-chacha12-u64-v1`: ChaCha12, explicit u64 random indices and portable Wilson draws. This deliberately changes the old SmallRng streams; version-1 seeds must not be claimed to reproduce protocol-2 output. The native selected-plan provenance/lineage records protocol identity. The browser boundary excludes wall-clock variation by recording NDJSON runtime zero (unmeasured); native standalone calls still measure runtime. Input validation rejects empty/asymmetric/disconnected graphs, duplicate/self/out-of-range arcs, mismatched/negative/overflowing populations, malformed share arrays and the one-plan configuration that could panic. Final validity is measured rather than inferred from frontier rank.

Limits: 3 MiB RCTX, 10,000 units, 100,000 arcs, 500 districts, 2–1,000 plans, 0–1,000 generations; at most 50 million unit-plan-generation entries and ten million population-square-generation entries. Optional share objectives use total-population weighting and are proxies, not election-count, VAP-weighted or legal VRA measurements. Protected districts and edge weights are unused by the current native kernel. This is a heuristic nondominated frontier among generated candidates, not a proof of global Pareto optimality. Selected-frontier native package replay, audit adoption and supplied-geometry maps are described below. Richer analysis remains incomplete.

These small budgets do not establish algorithm convergence. The browser displayed the maximum u64 seed and showed passing and failing final constraints; project/UI request, busy/freshness and exact context retention checks passed. No public deployment has been updated.

### Research ensemble diagnostics backend (2026-10-06)

`validate-research-ensemble` accepts `chains_jsonl` (plain filename to original JSONL text), optional original `enacted_json`, `rhat_threshold` and `ess_min`. It calls the shared in-memory `bisect_analysis::research_ensemble` validator, also used by the native research CLI. Output retains exact native `validate-ensemble.json` report text, structured per-metric diagnostics, source hashes and threshold settings. Equal-length chains must record every metric at every step; empty metric sets and duplicate metric keys are rejected. Input is bounded to 3 MiB, 4–32 chains, 5,000 steps per chain and 64 metrics with names at most 120 bytes. A conservative pooled-sample-squared work bound limits worst-case ESS autocorrelation work.

The native method concatenates traces in lexicographic filename order for ESS. This preserves CLI behavior and does not calculate separate chain-boundary corrections. `EssRecord.below_threshold` uses the native fixed 100 cutoff; `passes_thresholds` uses the supplied ESS minimum. Burn-in removal and thinning are practitioner-supplied. The report does not authenticate ensembles, generate MCMC samples, measure partition-space Hamming autocorrelation, establish optimality or certify legal validity.

### Minimum-rectangle tie policy correction (local, unpublished)

The native length_width_ratio measurement previously used the first strictly smallest-area hull-edge box after rotating absolute coordinates. Equal-area boxes can have different aspect ratios: a 3-4-5 right triangle has 4-by-3 and 5-by-2.4 minimum-area rectangles. Roundoff could select different boxes after translating the same shape. The shared native/WASM measurement now rotates relative coordinates and selects the minimum aspect ratio among area ties within a coordinate-roundoff tolerance (64 times machine epsilon, scaled by box area plus coordinate magnitude times span). Reports record length_width_method as minimum-area-hull-edge-box-minimum-aspect-roundoff-ties-v1; the source-record table displays it.

This changes legacy ratios for ambiguous or roundoff-close minimum rectangles. It is a declared tie convention, not a claim that all minimum-area rectangles have the same elongation. The implementation scans hull vertices for each edge (quadratic work), correcting the previous linear rotating-calipers description. Existing geometry work bounds continue to apply. Input quantization and projection remain material limitations.

### Hull-reduced minimum-circle search v2 (local, unpublished)

Exact Reock now uses convex-hull vertices, since a circle containing the hull also contains the polygon. A containing diameter circle ends the search: its endpoints impose a radius lower bound that the circle attains. Otherwise pair/triple candidate search remains, with candidates no smaller than the best circle pruned. Circumcenters use support-relative coordinates rather than squared absolute coordinates, and collinearity requires zero determinant rather than a fixed absolute threshold. Containment uses a relative floating-point tolerance. Small or translated polygons can therefore differ numerically from legacy reports.

The named method is convex-hull-diameter-proof-pruned-vertex-circles-v2. A conservative charged-work counter covers hull setup, circle candidates and containment scans, shared across districts; crossing 50 million rejects the operation before further search. Reports expose exact_reock_work_charged rather than the previous n^4 preflight estimate. The comparison table reads old work-bound metadata for reopened legacy reports. Actual wall-clock cost is not certified by this model. Native callers without a supplied limit retain unrestricted operation.

The worst-case search remains quartic after hull reduction; this is not a full statewide scaling solution. Existing 3 MiB source, topology and dissolve budgets remain. The prior 100-vertex circular fixture can now run via a diameter proof instead of failing its pessimistic n^4 bound. A large odd-vertex circle exercises the work-cap rejection when no diameter circle contains all vertices. No geometry is silently simplified.

Verification: 44 native compactness tests pass, including 100 optimized/exhaustive candidate-search comparisons, analytic tiny acute triangles that require circumcircles, translation/scale cases and work rejection. Twenty-one native/WASM results and twenty-one native report byte matches pass with 37 rejected requests. ### Spatially indexed ring validation (local, unpublished)

The bounded shared geometry reader uses an R-tree broad phase for ring self-intersection checks. It charges index preparation proportional to segment count times its binary-log level estimate and each returned candidate, then uses the same native segment intersection predicate and adjacency exclusions as the former exhaustive check. Disjoint envelopes cannot intersect. This retains the existing ring acceptance convention; it does not repair geometry or introduce an exact-arithmetic topology certificate. ### Optional balanced dissolve (local, unpublished)

Plan compactness accepts dissolve_method=balanced. Sequential remains the default and omitting the option preserves earlier report fields. The balanced reader groups units by district, keeps their input sequence, then merges adjacent pairs in rounds, carrying any unpaired item to the next round. It uses the existing native BooleanOps union and metric code. Union order can change floating-point geometry and scores; reports explicitly record balanced-input-order-pairs-indexed-work-v1. This is an opt-in computational method, not a new compactness formula or an optimality certificate. The file-backed native CLI loader is not changed.

Before each balanced union, an indexed broad phase counts potential cross-input segment events. The shared 50-million charged-work model covers index setup, returned candidates and a sweep estimate proportional to (segments + candidates) times binary-log levels, with a factor of three. It is a cost model, not a wall-clock, allocation or exact complexity certificate. Existing source, position, intermediate-output and topology limits remain. No coordinate is rounded or simplified. The balanced strategy can reduce repeated accumulation cost, but it is not uniformly faster for every input.

The workbench exposes Sequential and Balanced pairs, retains the selected mode in local projects, includes it only when explicitly selected in requests, disables the choice while running and invalidates computed exports on edits. Opening a project retains the setting without analysis. The source record displays the recorded method or the legacy sequential default. Missing/invalid method values are handled by the shared request schema and project validator.

### Native county-weight semantics correction (local, unpublished)

Review of configuration-driven execution found that the WASM county path used physical boundary multiplied by max(alpha, 1), while native `SubdivisionWeighter::county_only` uses boundary multiplied by 1 + alpha on same-county edges when alpha exceeds 1e-10. The old rule gave alpha 2 a factor of 2 instead of 3, and ignored fractional alpha below 1. The browser engine now applies the native formula and threshold, both when checking finite weighted totals and when building algorithm edge costs. Cross-county edges retain their physical lengths. Other weight modes keep their existing behavior.

County results now record `native-county-additive-v1` weighting evidence, including alpha, effective same-county multiplier, physical-boundary baseline, five-digit GEOID county identity and disabled-signal threshold. Prior county assignments/scores can differ from recomputed results; the new evidence identifies the corrected rule. Existing saved plans remain their recorded assignments and are not silently regenerated.

The dedicated gate uses the actual native CLI SubdivisionWeighter to create the independent edge-weight oracle. Sixteen native/WASM cases cover single/multi search and alpha 0, 1e-11, 1e-10, 1.1e-10, 0.5, 1, 2 and 100. Assignments match a geographic engine control supplied with the native oracle edges, and both weighted cut totals and physical cut totals match independent sums. Same/cross-county edges and evidence are checked. A finite physical-total case that overflows only under the corrected additive weighting is rejected by native and WASM; a valid run succeeds afterward. Evidence: `target/county-weights-wasm/evidence.json`. Existing engine gate passes 21 executions; plan export retains seven native/WASM matches and ten rejected cases. The build now compiles/runs the native county oracle and typed engine reference before this gate.

Configuration-driven execution remains pending. Further observed mapping questions must be resolved from source: native build assigns the converted algorithm into a fresh StateConfig but currently does not apply YAML balance_tolerance; the native run uses a fractional effective tolerance, while YAML/browser options declare percent. YAML area_swing is a margin (default 0.10), while the existing WASM option is a ratio (default 1.10). YAML's absent fixed seed must not silently become a browser seed. Native minority edge weighting also needs an explicit matching implementation/input path before mapping vra-aligned configurations. ### YAML AreaSection multiplier correction (local, unpublished)

The area engine consumes an imbalance multiplier: at the root each side must have at most 0.5 * area_swing of the total area. Thus 1.10 allows a 45%-55% split. Native YAML incorrectly defaulted to 0.10 and forwarded it unchanged, making the lower area bound exceed the upper bound. Shared compositor resolution now defaults to 1.10, matching native direct-run defaults and the browser engine, and rejects nonfinite values or multipliers outside [1, 2]. Existing declarations such as 0.10 or 0.25 must be edited to the intended multiplier; they are not automatically reinterpreted. Source files and saved assignments remain intact. Native AreaSection execution also guards the multiplier when area constraints are active. WASM options, laboratory input and project validation now accept the exact-balance multiplier 1.

The new config_area_reference executes native YAML conversion and the actual pure-Rust AreaSection routine. Ten cases cover single/multi search and omitted, 1, 1.25, 1.9 and 2 multipliers, comparing complete WASM assignments and cut values while independently summing both root areas and checking their bounds. Evidence is target/config-area-wasm/evidence.json. The shared configuration gate passes 61 native/WASM comparisons with 16 three-way rejections, including four fractional-margin/out-of-range cases. Template parity passes 60 comparisons and 17 rejections, the native configuration suite passes 47 tests, and the existing engine gate passes 21 runs. Laboratory project roundtrips pass against dist/wasm-national assets; dist/wasm-comparison is a practitioner-only tree without catalog.json. The added endpoint project-validation assertions run against current source. Seed semantics, minority weighting, configuration-driven execution and the wider inventory remain unfinished. No deployment occurred.

### Pinned tutorial-data checks

Choose **Check pinned tutorial data**, supply the tutorial name and checksum document, and select local files or their containing repository folder. Folder paths are relative to the selected root; only files referenced by the supplied checksum document are read. Rust SHA-256 streams binary files in 1 MiB chunks inside the browser worker. There is no aggregate file-byte cap or whole-file buffering. The checksum document is capped at 512 KiB and 2,000 relative file references. Unsafe paths and duplicate selections are rejected. No source URL is fetched and no path grants filesystem access.

Native schema, case-insensitive hash comparison, read errors, drift and missing-file behavior are retained. Missing files keep native exit code 0 but have visible **files missing** status. Expected tract counts remain informational and retain exact u64 values; neither CLI nor browser recomputes them. Hash matching proves only that selected bytes match supplied pins. The checked-in Vermont checksum document currently contains `PIN_ON_FIRST_RUN` placeholders; supplied files will mismatch these until a maintainer legitimately pins them.

Projects preserve the exact checksum source and report. Large binary inputs are not embedded or reopened by path. ## Label build progress transport

The WASM ABI adds an optional `env.bisect_progress` host callback alongside the existing random-byte import. `instantiateEngine.execute(request, {onProgress})` delivers independent parsed checkpoints synchronously before execution continues. A state checkpoint contains its completed success/failure row and exact newly generated file bytes; a year checkpoint contains the completed summary/index and registry snapshot. Each event includes an ordered sequence, label and SHA-256 of the resolved request inputs. That binding detects changed input identity; it does not authenticate source truth or prove legal compliance. No checkpoint marks an unfinished year built.

Worker messages relay each checkpoint with the active run ID before the final result. A listener failure returns an error through the ABI, releases input memory and permits another execution. Reentrant execution/hashing from inside a callback is rejected. Consumers can retain completed deltas outside the worker; changing a parsed event cannot mutate engine output. Native direct calls use a no-op emitter and retain their existing result behavior.

The workbench displays and saves received checkpoints and retains completed outputs on cancellation. Automatic resume and broad national capacity remain unfinished; opening a project is inert and a new explicit Run starts a fresh build. Checkpoint events are bounded to 64 MiB and imports remain allowlisted. New host code accepts older modules without the progress import, while older host code correctly rejects a module with an unsupported import.

Validation: five ordered request-bound checkpoints match final state files/year indexes exactly. Tests cover a changed request identity, mixed failure/success progress, retained deltas after a simulated listener stop, listener-error recovery, reentrancy rejection, mutation isolation and run-ID worker relay. ## Portable build archives above the ordinary project limit

## Native fallback manifest boundary

Both commission WASM operations accept an optional closed `fallback` object containing bounded label/year strings. If the supplied manifest is absent or cannot deserialize as the native PlanManifest, an explicitly supplied fallback creates the same default manifest as native Report. Without that explicit fallback, missing/invalid manifests continue to reject. Valid native manifests always take precedence. Native CLI and WASM share the minimal manifest constructor. Fallback does not repair missing required analysis, referenced context/certificate errors, unsafe report paths or unexpected report files.

Results record `manifest_resolution` with `fallback_used` and source status supplied/missing/invalid. The result table displays this separately from recorded claims; older results without that metadata display Not recorded. Synthesized metadata does not recover provenance. Original malformed/invalid-UTF-8 bytes remain hashed when present; a missing manifest has no source hash. Audit-only accepts either original JSON text or original byte vectors (one representation only), allowing exact corrupt-byte retention at this boundary. Fallback label/year are limited to 200 UTF-8 bytes and manifest sources to 16 MiB. Full report package limits remain unchanged.

Five actual CLI full JSON/HTML/companion runs and five actual CLI audit-only runs match WASM byte for byte, normalizing only the native report clock. Cases cover missing manifest, malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8, a typed-field failure and a complete valid manifest that overrides fallback metadata, with exact large integers retained. Four invalid fallback/source representation/bound requests reject. Tests also require fallback to leave context and required-analysis failures fatal and check the fallback status table. ### Registry snapshot reconciliation ABI

`reconcile-label-registry` accepts an `analyzed` or `reported` stage, the original `source_registry_json` and recorded `source_registry_sha256`, `current_registry_json`, `proposed_registry_json`, the exact current `upstream_index_json`, and `generated_index_json`. It first checks the original snapshot hash. The proposal must equal exactly the shared native stage transition on that original snapshot; arbitrary added/deleted labels or changed arrays are rejected. The current build index (analysis) or analysis index (reporting) must match the generated index's raw-byte chain hash and label/year. Changed upstream bytes, including whitespace, require rerunning the stage. Current native stage prerequisites are enforced.

The operation reapplies only that stage to the supplied current registry, preserving concurrently added labels, other years, array order and duplicates. It returns `.bisect` text, source/current/proposed registry hashes, upstream and generated index paths/hashes, and the merged registry hash. Stage records retain native command-completion semantics, including partial outcomes. No filesystem is read or written, and no authentication is established. A later disk applicator must recheck the current registry and upstream hashes before writing; this operation alone cannot prevent a change after the selected snapshot was read.

This is a local foundation for project/repository merging. The workbench exposes reconciliation with separate draft, current registry and current upstream index selectors. Fresh registry-aware analysis and report results can prepare an exact draft; this does not run reconciliation automatically. Users must select the actual current snapshots and Run explicitly. Save/Open retains all sources; opening an imported result does not enable export until a fresh Run. Download validates the reconciled registry bytes and hash and produces `.bisect`. Input changes invalidate exports. Artifact-file collision handling, coordinated application to local disk, and larger archive delivery remain unfinished. The workbench now exposes 79 operations.

### Repository stage package preparation

`reconcile-label-package` extends registry reconciliation to text artifacts. Its input contains `reconciliation` (the registry reconciliation input above), `current_files` and `generated_files` (relative path to exact text), `generated_file_sha256` (one digest per generated file), and `expected_file_sha256` (one expectation per generated non-registry file). An expectation of `null` requires that the current file is absent. A digest requires that the current file exists and has exactly those bytes. Expectations must come from the stage's intended baseline; substituting freshly observed hashes would discard the ability to detect intervening changes.

The package's current registry and upstream index must equal the selected reconciliation snapshots. Its generated registry and index must equal the proposed registry and generated stage index. Generated analysis paths must belong to indexed states and supported native filenames. Generated report files must exactly match the native report index inventory. The operation rejects mismatched hashes, missing expectations, changed/deleted/new artifacts, unsafe paths, Windows reserved names, case collisions and file/directory collisions. Only after all checks does it return a prepared map with the reconciled registry, generated artifacts, and unchanged unrelated files. No caller input or filesystem is mutated. It also returns the change list and all current/output hashes. Repeated preparation with matching current expectations is idempotent.

Each input/output file map is limited to 2,000 text files and 25 MiB; repository paths are at most 512 ASCII bytes with segments at most 200 bytes. The workbench's complete source JSON is also limited to 25 MiB. Binary data, larger archives, folder-based source collection, automatic stage-to-package handoff and coordinated disk installation remain unfinished. These checks establish byte integrity and snapshot conflict detection, not authenticated metrics or atomic application. A disk applicator must recheck every original current file and generated-file absence expectation under an appropriate locking/installation protocol.

The workbench exposes **Prepare repository stage package**: select the source JSON, Run explicitly, inspect artifact additions/replacements, and download the prepared repository ZIP. Imported project results are inert; fresh execution is required to enable export. Source changes invalidate the result, and async source/export operations reject stale project revisions. Save/Open retains the exact selected source and result. ZIP export rechecks every output hash, preserves UTF-8 bytes and writes no executable entries. The workbench now exposes 80 operations; changes are local and unpublished.

### ILP model-artifact audit ABI

`audit-ilp-artifacts` accepts `input.reports` (portable relative report path to exact JSON text), `models_base64` (portable relative model path to exact binary bytes encoded as base64), and optional `summary_json` (a previously saved native audit summary). ### Public RPLAN package verification ABI

`verify-rplan-package` accepts `input.manifest_json` and `files_base64` (portable relative path to selected binary bytes). Supported manifest schemas are `u20-public-example-manifest-v1` and `benchmark-rplan-package-manifest-v1`. The new shared `rplan_audit::package_verification` kernel checks every listed file's exact SHA-256, accepts the native uppercase-digest convention, selects the first native `plan`, `context`, and `certificate` role entries, parses their exact bytes, and invokes the native audit-certificate content and plan/context binding verifier. The native CLI's existing golden/benchmark package branch delegates to this same kernel; its filesystem adapter retains streamed file hashing and root-relative resolution. General BISECT manifest replay and assignment-only verification remain unported separate branches.

The browser adapter consults only selected bytes. Missing selected files, changed hashes, missing roles, invalid package manifests and certificate-binding failures produce an inspectable failed result with a native-equivalent exit code. Selected paths and manifest paths are constrained to portable relative ASCII names; traversal, drive/backslash paths, dangerous components, duplicate declarations and case collisions are rejected. Limits: 1 MiB manifest, 100 selected/declared files and 16 MiB decoded file bytes. Selected files beyond the declared manifest inventory receive disclosed hashes but are not counted as manifest-verified files. No referenced filesystem path or URL is opened.

Output schema `bisect-rplan-package-verification-v1` contains status, native exit code, error, manifest/source hashes and the shared receipt: declared file count, selected role paths, certificate ID/content hash, bound plan/context hashes and the certificate's recorded audit result. A valid certificate can record **failed** audit checks while its content and bindings still verify; this operation preserves that result and does not turn it into a passed audit. Package hashes and role labels are supplied claims, and successful verification does not authenticate the author, independently recompute recorded checks, replay solver work or establish legal validity.

The workbench exposes **Verify public RPLAN package**, bringing its operation count to 82. ### Native verification assignment comparison

`compare-verify-assignments` accepts `input.original_json`, `reference_json` and `min_similarity`. Both sources are exact JSON objects mapping unit identifiers to integer district numbers. The shared `bisect_report::assignment_verification::assignment_agreement` is now used by native Verify's assignments-only calculation and its replay similarity helper. It preserves literal district numbers, including zero, and uses matching assignments divided by **the larger map size**. Native CLI calls this Jaccard similarity; it is not a set-union denominator or a district-relabeling similarity. The receipt additionally exposes original/reference counts, matches, units unique to each source and shared units with changed districts.

An empty original returns `unavailable` with comparison exit code 1, matching the native assignments-only early abort. An empty reference has similarity zero and follows the supplied threshold comparison. Finite thresholds outside 0–1 preserve native behavior, so a zero or negative threshold may accept zero similarity for a nonempty original; thresholds over 1 cannot pass. These values are disclosed, not silently clamped. Limits: two nonempty JSON texts up to 8 MiB each; at most one million units per source, 240 UTF-8 bytes per unit identifier and unsigned wasm32 district range. Invalid JSON or district types/range are rejected. Browser source loading uses strict UTF-8 and rejects ambiguous duplicate JSON keys before saving exact bytes.

### Replay a selected engine run

Select **Replay saved engine run** in the practitioner workbench. Load original
unit-to-district assignment JSON and a run artifact containing `kind` and its
complete payload. `engine` and `engine-build` use `request` containing the
prepared graph, engine options and optional auxiliary sources. `configured`
and `configured-build` use `input` containing the YAML text, prepared graph and
configured-run fields. `multiscale` and `multiscale-build` use `input` containing
the complete multiscale request, including fine graphs and adaptation settings.
Build variants repeat the native population retry policy.

Run explicitly to regenerate assignments. The receipt retains the generated
result, exact optional seed, input hashes, current build identity, comparison
threshold and native literal district agreement. District labels are compared
as supplied. Missing seeds retain native behavior and do not establish
deterministic replay. Empty originals stop before execution. Failed executions
remain inspectable and distinguish execution started from execution completed.

Sources total at most 16 MiB, with original assignments at most 8 MiB. Save/Open
preserves sources within existing project limits; opening does not execute or
enable fresh receipt download. Editing inputs invalidates the result. This
operation does not compose manifest prechecks or reproduce native filesystem
discovery and binary provenance checks. This addition is local and undeployed.


After a configuration run completes, **Prepare accepted run replay** fills the
replay sources from its effective engine request and generated assignments.
Then press **Run**. This replays the accepted attempt with its recorded seed;
it does not repeat the original build's retry sequence. A fresh completed run
is required, so opening a saved result alone cannot enable this handoff.


### Check a manifest before replay

**Check manifest then replay selected run** displays both manifest/package and
replay source panels. One explicit Run checks recorded ILP summary/model files
and certificate bindings in native order, then replays the selected run and
compares the selected original assignments. Failed prechecks stop replay.
Absent sidecar records remain `not-recorded` and permit replay. Combined sources
are limited to 16 MiB. Opening a saved project stays inert; source or threshold
edits invalidate its fresh receipt. Download retains both stage receipts.

Before replay, correspondence checks compare state, year, district count,
exact optional seed, tolerance and the original assignment universe against the
manifest. Configured inputs also check chamber. Recorded RPLAN assignments and
engine options are compared when present. Prepared-graph provenance checks both
the graph hash and actual RCTX contents through the native export kernel.
A mismatch returns `binding-failed` without starting the engine.

`manifest_to_run_binding` is `verified` when the recorded plan, options and
prepared context and supplied auxiliary inputs bind. Missing
recorded evidence yields `partial`; empty
originals yield `unavailable`. Stage details distinguish these outcomes. For
builds whose seed changed during retries, select the accepted-attempt replay.
Complete native Verify discovery, fetching and binary provenance remain pending. This local operation has not been deployed.


Auxiliary correspondence reports demographics, character, partisan and election
inputs separately. Demographic fractions and raw counts bind through the native
context export's full input hash and demographic fields. Character, partisan
and election inputs require matching recorded RPLAN input provenance plus the
native context/source hashes. Missing input provenance stays partial. Recorded
numeric values are normalized through native typed schemas, so equivalent JSON
spellings such as `0` and `0.0` compare consistently without rounding u64 seeds.
Source descriptions are retained claims; correspondence does not authenticate
Census, election, LODES or ACS observations.


Multiscale correspondence binds coarse/fine inputs and fixed/adaptive settings
through recorded typed input provenance and the native context input hash.
Tract contexts reconstruct physical boundaries from the prepared graph.
Block-group artifacts may include `fine_edges` beside `kind` and `input`:

```json
{"kind":"multiscale","input":{},"fine_edges":[[0,1,100.0]]}
```

Replace placeholders with the complete saved inputs and ordered physical edge
list. That list reconstructs the exact native fine context; its order participates
in the native boundary evidence hash. It supplies audit context evidence and is
not used by sampler generation. Missing block-group boundaries keep correspondence
partial while replay remains available. Changed recorded inputs or context/edge
evidence stop execution. Both `multiscale` and `multiscale-build` accept this field.
Generated report manifests now preserve multiscale producer seed and tolerance.

An observed seedless sampling fixture yields an empty district in both native
and WASM execution; both native exporters reject it. A matching replay receipt
is assignment agreement, not proof that the sampled plan satisfies audit rules.

### Loaded WASM artifact identity (local development)

The ABI loader copies the supplied BufferSource, then hashes and compiles the

caller-supplied runtime_artifact. The fresh receipt retains an advisory literal
hash comparison using the shared native Verify sentinel and equality rules.

identity remains unavailable. Mismatch does not change native Doctor version
compatibility exit behavior. Direct ABI callers provide identity metadata as
claims; only the browser host measures the actual loaded module.

or version equality does not attest equivalent behavior, original execution,
source authenticity or legal validity. No manifest URL or executable is fetched.
A failed worker initialization clears the previous engine so it cannot continue
under a failed identity/integrity check. This extends manifest inspection;
full native Verify replay/binary orchestration remains incomplete. Local only.

### Direct gzip LODES preparation (2026-10-08)

The LODES operation now accepts exactly one csv_text or source_base64 input.
Base64 sources may hold plain CSV or gzip: magic bytes select the decoder,
independent of filename. Existing plain CSV requests remain supported. Gzip
streams through the same single-member flate2 decoder used by native Fetch and
then through the shared aggregator. Rust hashes and counts decoded bytes while
reading; JS does not allocate an expanded source string. The decoder checks
checksum and truncation. Consistent with native Fetch, additional gzip members
or bytes after the first member are not aggregated; the source hash still covers
the complete original file. This behavior is disclosed in the receipt.

The receipt separates source_sha256/source_byte_length/source_encoding from
decoded_sha256/decoded_byte_length and the existing aggregate CSV digest. Plain
CSV source and decoded hashes are identical. Inputs remain bounded to 16 MiB
of original bytes; gzip expansion is bounded to 128 MiB with an explicit error.
The bounds do not establish complete coverage for all real-state LODES files.
Large-source acquisition and persistence beyond these limits remain pending.

The workbench selects .csv or .csv.gz, retains original compressed bytes in
Save/Open, and sends those bytes to Rust only after an explicit Run. Corrupt
compressed sources can be retained as unverified source material; preparation
fails when the decoder reads them. Reopening does not decompress or execute.
The ordinary 25 MiB project cap still applies to the full saved project.

Evidence: four exact compiled native-host/WASM/native gzip file comparisons,
including a 20 MiB expanded fixture and concatenated-member native parity;
independent source/decoded/output hashes; three matching native corruption,
truncation and header failures; invalid/ambiguous source rejection and expansion
past 128 MiB. Plain LODES regressions and the full UI suite pass. Browser proof
shows 57,014 compressed bytes streamed into 20,971,618 decoded bytes with a ready
economic input. This fixture validates the streaming path, not real-state source
coverage. These changes remain local and unpublished.

the public Cloudflare deployment remains unchanged.


### Native derived Fetch data packages (2026-10-08)

After a fresh ACS housing or LODES preparation, select native targets and run
`prepare-fetch-data-package` explicitly. The package builder rebuilds CSV from
the retained source bytes through the shared parser, binds its state/year to
the selected Fetch item, and returns the native relative target and completion
marker. Download derived data ZIP exports those two files after checking their
SHA-256 hashes. Open project remains inert; imported results cannot enable this
export until rerun. Force is saved and changing it invalidates the result.

Native completion writes exactly the three bytes `done`. Selected target plus
marker skips conversion unless force is set; marker alone does not skip.
The typed operation also accepts an explicit `unavailable404` claim to reproduce
native header-only CSV plus marker. That claim does not perform or verify an
HTTP request. A native completion marker can accompany unavailable data and
does not establish usable inputs or certify a plan.

The builder does not install files, inspect actual disk targets, implement the
raw FLETCH cache, or run the engine. Its ZIP bound is 128 MiB; ordinary project
persistence still has its separate 25 MiB envelope. Custom native paths outside
the ZIP exporter's allowed character set remain unsupported. TIGER, PL94,
adjacency, school, EIA and full Fetch/state orchestration remain unfinished.

The package parity gate compares compiled native-host and WASM receipts, then
serves local fixture responses to actual native `download_items` for all three
source kinds and both HTTP200/404. Those six cases compare exact CSV and marker
bytes and native `is_done`. It also checks incremental skip/force, marker-only
inventory, scope rejection, source preservation and hash rejection. An independent
Python ZIP reader checks all six archives without extracting them: exact bytes,
CRC, SHA-256 and non-executable permissions. Localhost permission is required
for the native HTTP fixture; public-network success is not inferred from it.
The full UI suite checks inert Open, exact requests, busy controls, fresh ZIP
bytes, force invalidation and handoff without automatic execution.
The local browser check opened the retained ACS fixture inertly, ran preparation,
selected native targets, ran the package builder, and invoked the enabled ZIP
export. Its receipt shows relative target/marker paths, both hashes and
`installation_performed: false`; proof: `target/wasm-fetch-data-package.png`.
These changes remain local and unpublished.

### Public ACS/LODES acquisition handoff (2026-10-08)

The Fetch workbench now offers a source selector after a fresh source-plan Run.
Only the exact native public ACS housing and LODES WAC/OD URLs for the selected
known state/year are eligible. Imported results remain unverified and cannot
trigger acquisition. Download is an explicit separate action. The fetch uses
CORS mode, credentials omit, redirects error and no-referrer; requests are never
triggered by Open, autosave or conversion. Workbench CSP adds only the two Census
hosts to connect-src. Script, worker, object and other protections remain scoped.

Census changed its data-query policy in May 2026: ACS requests now require a key.
The password field supplies the key only for the explicit ACS request and clears
when download starts. LODES does not require that field. The key is excluded from
source-plan URLs, receipts, projects and diagnostics; raw fetch exceptions are
replaced with a message that does not contain the request URL. The browser sends
the key only to its fixed Census API endpoint. Native Fetch host key handling
still requires an update; the shared planner deliberately does not store keys.
Provider reference: https://www.census.gov/library/video/2026/adrm/requesting-a-census-data-api-key.html

Successful acquisition retains exact browser-exposed response bytes, a SHA-256
receipt and selected state/year metadata. HTTP transfer decoding may occur in
the browser; this hash identifies the bytes exposed to the application, not an
independent publisher checksum or raw wire stream. Sources enter the existing
ACS/LODES preparation panels. Conversion and any engine run require explicit Run.
Metadata persists as fetchAcquisitionReceipt; source bytes are stored once in
the preparation inputs. Opening a saved receipt treats it as recorded metadata.

Response headers and streamed body enforce a 16 MiB limit. HTTP404 records
unavailable and installs no input or marker; other HTTP errors, redirections,
malformed ACS JSON and invalid UTF-8 reject the handoff. Cancellation and project
revision changes discard pending results. No disk installation, cache activation,
empty-file/done-marker materialization, local-first/GitHub fallback or other
source type acquisition is implemented by this action. Full Fetch/FLETCH
orchestration and real sources exceeding current bounds remain unfinished.

Evidence: fixture HTTP ACS/gzip responses pass exact byte/hash checks and actual
compiled WASM preparation, with source/receipt project roundtrips. Tests reject
unexpected destinations, key persistence/leaking network errors, pre-aborted
requests, invalid JSON, HTTP failures, redirects and declared/streamed oversize
responses. Full UI tests pass fresh-only acquisition, busy guards, no Open
requests, no automatic worker execution, cancel/stale-result rejection and 404.
Live browser ACS and LODES requests failed; a terminal request also could not
resolve api.census.gov. No real external download success is claimed. Validation
against a working network and a user-supplied Census key remains open. Changes

### Shared FLETCH cache report boundary

`bisect-core::fletch_cache` now owns the native BISECT cache-index report types and projection. The CLI still reads and validates the cache manifest through pinned `fletch-core`, builds its cache index, and supplies that library's gate counts to the shared projection. This boundary has no filesystem or network operations and compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

The projection preserves native last-entry-per-dataset selection, separate upstream gate counts, missing rows, unexpected rows, sorting, schema identifiers, and exact u64 byte values. An empty expected registry retains the upstream gate's zero unexpected count while the BISECT report still labels existing entries as unexpected rows. Regression fixtures cover this distinction and byte values above JavaScript's exact integer range.

This is preparation for the browser cache-index workflow. Manifest import, upstream validation parity in the browser, toolkit controls, and report download remain to be implemented. A saved `verified` flag represents manifest evidence; this report does not re-hash cached files or certify election plans. The FLETCH inventory entries therefore remain pending.

Validation: two shared projection tests and the existing native cache-index regression pass. The shared crate passes the WASM target compile check. The initial broad CLI test build exhausted compiler memory; the focused binary test passed with one build job.


### FLETCH cache manifest WASM operation

`inspect-fletch-cache` accepts a Fetch source selection and selected cache manifest text. It derives expected source IDs from the shared native source planner and uses the shared cache report projection. Manifest schema, typed fields, SHA256 prefix/length validation, and gate count semantics follow pinned FLETCH `7c7aacd4fbc8753299e2fc3181368d2cc6d90337`. As in native FLETCH, the hash check does not require hexadecimal digits. The browser input is capped at 8 MiB and rejects total byte-count overflow explicitly.

### Fresh FLETCH cache file verification in WASM

The toolkit now exposes **Verify selected FLETCH cache files**. Users select a cache manifest and either its object folder or individual files, then explicitly Run. The worker first validates every manifest-relative path in Rust, then streams only referenced selected files through the WASM SHA256 hasher in chunks of at most 1 MiB. Verification compares both the observed hash and byte count with the manifest using pinned native immutable-policy semantics. Saved `verified` flags do not determine the result. Files absent from the selection are reported missing; this does not assert absence from disk. Folder selection removes its top container name; paths are normalized to forward slashes and matched with exact case. Individual selections use filenames, so nested object paths require folder selection.

Manifest input is limited to 8 MiB and 2,000 entries; selection accepts at most 10,000 file references. Traversal, absolute/drive paths, empty or dot components, NUL and paths exceeding 1,024 UTF-8 bytes are rejected before hashing. Duplicate selected paths are rejected. Unreferenced selected files are never read. Manifest cache-root and report absolute-path strings are informational portable spellings and are never opened. A failed or shortened read rejects the operation without a verification receipt; the same engine instance can subsequently hash again. Cancellation uses the existing worker termination flow.

Results display verified, missing and mismatch counts, per-file status, actual hashes and exact decimal byte counts. Fresh results enable **Download native verification report**, preserving Rust's exact u64 JSON numbers without a JavaScript numeric roundtrip. Save/Open retains the original manifest and result, but selected File references remain session-only. Open is inert, clears selected files, and marks restored results unverified; users must reselect files and Run to enable the report download. Busy guards prevent selection changes during verification.

### Native cache-manifest merge boundary

`merge-fletch-cache-manifest` is now a WASM ABI operation. It accepts `cache_manifest_json` (the original manifest text) and `entries_json` (a JSON array of typed native CacheEntry records). Shared Rust code implements pinned FLETCH `upsert_cache_manifest_entries`: validate the base, replace the first existing matching **cache_key** in place, append unmatched keys, apply updates in order, retain any other duplicate base keys, preserve the cache root and reset `generated_by` to `fletch-core/0.1.0`. Dataset ID is not the merge key. Defaults, optional/retry fields, native SHA-prefix/length validation and unknown-field acceptance follow the pinned native contract.

The result carries exact native pretty-printed manifest bytes in `manifest_json`, separate input SHA256 identities, an entry count and explicit metadata-only scope. It preserves u64 fields without passing them through JavaScript numbers. Unlike cache-index summarization, merging does not sum byte counts, so valid entries whose aggregate bytes exceed u64 remain mergeable, as in upstream FLETCH. Paths and URLs remain inert strings, including strings that a subsequent object-verification operation would reject. Saved verification flags are copied as claims and are never upgraded by the merge.

Browser limits are 8 MiB and 2,000 entries per input, 2,000 entries after merging and 16 MiB for serialized output. Entry limits are checked before the native linear key searches. ### Immutable cache-first and offline acquisition

`resolve-fletch-cache-request` ports the pinned native no-header HTTP `fetch_to_cache` immutable decision branch and `cache_hit_outcome`. It uses the same cache-key bytes as native staging. A fresh observed body hash/size is compared with the first trusted entry matching key/dataset/URL and with an optional expected digest. Matched historical timestamps, verification flags, retry counts and last retry error are preserved; the current attempt records zero attempts/retries. Without matched trust, the native requested timestamp or observed modified timestamp is used. Exact u64 values remain strings/native JSON text. Missing or forcibly bypassed objects reject offline with native error text; online misses and forced bypass return an acquisition decision without performing a request.

The Fetch panel offers provider download (default), cache-first download-on-miss and cache-only offline modes, plus explicit refresh/bypass. Cache lookup and actual-body hashing run through cancellable WASM workers; an IndexedDB row/Blob is read together. The browser adapter currently reuses indexed toolkit objects under immutable/no-header HTTP semantics. Unindexed orphan bodies require explicit staging because this store has no filesystem mtime to invent. A corrupt cache hit rejects without an implicit provider fallback. Fresh cached bytes pass the existing ACS/LODES readers or original ZIP extraction and select preparation inputs; they do not run the engine or implicitly update the cache. ACS cache hits do not require a provider API key. Offline never makes a provider request; refresh cannot use existing bytes offline. This is source-offline behavior: the application and its WASM/worker assets must already be available. Fully offline app-shell loading is not verified.

Cached receipts keep the existing receipt schema with explicit `transport: browser-cache`, native `cache_key` and `http_status: null`; they are distinct from HTTP acquisition claims. Source byte hashes and pinned scope remain validated. They roundtrip in projects as inert claims. Source access preferences/refresh reset on project Open, and Open never accesses the source cache or requests a provider. A separate session-only **Download cache-hit evidence** preserves exact native entry JSON, timestamp/retry history and zero-attempt status. Project/source revisions invalidate that export, and Open clears it; saved receipts do not become fresh evidence. The normal acquisition handler clears the Census key even when a cache hit makes it unnecessary.

Actual isolated Chrome exercises eight no-provider-request acquisitions across ACS, LODES WAC, TIGER and PL94, corrupt-body rejection without fallback, offline miss/forced bypass, cache-first miss/refresh provider requests without persistence, cancellation, receipt/project roundtrips and the real offline ACS UI, secret clearing, cache-hit evidence download/freshness and inert reopening. Existing network/acquired ZIP/project regressions pass. ### Provider retry and timeout controls

The source acquisition panel now offers a retry budget (0–10 additional attempts; default 0) and a per-request/body timeout (1–300,000 ms; default 30,000). The default timeout matches the pinned native blocking HTTP client. `fetch-network.js` follows the upstream retry loop's immediate retry of HTTP transport/status and body-read failures; it introduces no backoff. Partial failed bodies are discarded before a new attempt. The timeout spans response headers and body reads, and an explicit AbortController race enforces it even for an injected transport that ignores its signal. Cancellation stops further attempts and releases/cancels response readers. Browser URL/redirect and byte-limit guards are not retried; decoding, ZIP integrity and source parsing happen after transport and are not retried either. HTTP 404 uses the existing browser soft-unavailable receipt after the configured budget is exhausted; upstream FLETCH itself reports a final HTTP error.

Network receipts optionally retain an `attempt_status` object with attempts, retries and a sanitized last-retry category. Browser transport error strings are not byte-identical to reqwest's diagnostics; categories intentionally exclude provider URLs and ephemeral API keys. This history survives inert project Save/Open. Source access/retry/timeout controls reset on Open, which still performs no acquisition. Cache hits do not create network attempt metadata or need an ACS key. A successful or failed network acquisition does not implicitly persist into the source cache. Raw cache staging remains a separate fresh hashing/staging operation; importing the acquisition transport history into its native cache-entry fields is still unfinished.

`scripts/web/test_fetch_network.mjs` compares nine actual native owned-loopback HTTP outcomes with browser transport request/attempt/retry counts: first success, one/two retries, 401, 429, truncated body, exhaustion, soft 404, and timeout recovery. Both fixtures use a generous deadline and a substantially longer delayed first response so the timeout comparison does not depend on sub-100-ms client startup. Additional tests cover secret-free transport failures, nonretryable guards, cancellation, hung-transport deadline and option bounds. Acquisition tests cover retry receipts and inert/key-free project roundtrips, plus no retry after source parse failure. The actual isolated Chrome UI uses intercepted provider responses (no live provider request) to recover from 500 to 200, preserve the counted/sanitized receipt and leave source cache unchanged. Cancel during a held second request prevents the remainder of a three-retry budget and preserves the prior source and receipt. Evidence: `target/request-retry-native-validation.log`, `target/request-retry-browser-validation.log`, `target/request-retry-acquisition-regression.log`, `target/fletch-cache-browser/retry-ui.json` and `retry-cancel-ui.json`. The standalone build includes the native oracle/transport test; `-BrowserChecks` exercises the real UI.

Other freshness policies, bandwidth throttling, transport-history-to-cache-entry promotion, arbitrary source kinds/headers, full offline app loading and complete source/build orchestration remain unfinished. These changes are local and unpublished.


### Retained fetch attempt history in WASM staging

Raw staging accepts optional bounded native `fetch_history` metadata: u32 attempts and retries, plus a nullable diagnostic of up to 16 KiB UTF-8. Omitted history retains the existing one-attempt/zero-retry behavior. The WASM entry and export freshness check preserve supplied history exactly. History remains a recorded claim; hashing authenticates current bytes, not past requests.

Network acquisition selection carries its sanitized attempt receipt into staging. Cache loads retain their native entry history. Cache-hit acquisition receipts optionally retain the exact native entry text, checked against the receipt dataset, version, URL, key, hash and byte count; this preserves historical attempts without recording new network attempts. Projects and workbench archives preserve the history. The staging UI displays attempt/retry counts and retires history when the source or dataset/version/URL identity changes.

Validation: `test_fletch_history_wasm.mjs` compares actual native retry counts, checks zero/u32 bounds and diagnostics, project/archive round trips, acquisition handoff and invalid/mismatched history. Existing native staging comparisons and real browser cache tests cover persistence, history retention, cache-hit acquisition, and unchanged cancellation/quota/conflict guards. This work is local; it has not been deployed to Cloudflare. Full native Fetch orchestration and the remaining capability inventory are still incomplete.


### Browser cache freshness policies

Acquisition offers immutable reuse, always download, and maximum-age days through the WASM request resolver. Always download rejects offline reuse. Maximum age uses the origin-local object's actual write timestamp and the device clock, with future timestamps clamped to zero age and an inclusive millisecond age boundary. This projects native FLETCH filesystem-mtime policy onto browser storage; it does not use the native manifest's claimed fetch timestamp. Save and atomic restoration record a new object write time. Imported backup write-time claims cannot control restoration freshness. Legacy browser objects without that observation must be acquired again under maximum-age policy; immutable reuse remains compatible.

Policy controls reset on inert Open and are disabled during execution. A stale online object requests explicit acquisition without silently overwriting the cache; offline stale objects fail without provider access. Full application-shell offline loading, arbitrary source/header policies and native State/Fetch/build orchestration remain separate work.

Gates: `scripts/web/test_fletch_request_wasm.mjs` compares actual upstream native always-check, fresh/stale maximum-age and future-mtime outcomes, plus exact millisecond boundary and u32/time guards. The browser cache harness covers actual workers/IndexedDB policy reads, legacy/stale rejection, independent object/fetch timestamps, refreshed acquisition without cache mutation, maximum-age UI acquisition and policy reset. Local changes remain unpublished.

### Opt-in native round capture in WASM

Configured single runs and population-retry builds now offer **Capture native round events in memory**, default off. Shared native snapshot callsites emit into a scoped recorder while retaining their existing filesystem writer for native execution. WASM needs no pretend directory or virtual filesystem. Each event retains its chronological sequence, native name (including repeated names), exact index assignments, graph-order GEOID companion and SHA256 hashes. Coverage and exact-label agreement with the returned assignment are disclosed; partial snapshots, search candidates and zero-event engines are not presented as accepted complete histories. For retry builds only the accepted attempt's scoped result is returned.

The recorder permits 100,000 units, 128 events and two million total assignment entries. Invalid snapshots or bounds failures reject the run rather than silently truncate history; errors and guard destruction clear recording state. Native observers are thread-scoped; WASM executes serially. This is not proof of every native parallel/search callback or accepted recursive lineage. Canonical captured JSON has deterministic index order; filesystem HashMap JSON comparisons are semantic, not a byte-order equivalence claim.

The result panel exposes an event selector and exact assignment/index downloads. After a separate native RPLAN export, **Prepare recorded-round map** fills the selected complete snapshot and companion without executing anything. Choose matching local geometry and press Run explicitly. Partial events cannot be mapped through this handoff. Save/Open retains the capture option and sources/results; opening a project never runs the engine, and imported results require fresh execution before export or handoff. The bulk label-build capture extension is described below.

### Native COI weighting in configured Run (2026-10-09)

Configured Run and native TUI Run now accept an optional **community-of-interest weights JSON** file. The file maps unit IDs to finite nonnegative numeric weights. The shared native kernel applies `resolved_edge_weight * sqrt(weight_u * weight_v)` after geographic, county or other algorithm weighting. Missing units use one; unknown IDs are counted and ignored. Zero weights are supported. Native unweighted mode has an empty computed weight map, so COI has no effect there; the receipt states this rather than claiming changed edges. A weight file is a supplied input, not verified community provenance or a legal certificate.

The visible receipt records the exact selected UTF-8 JSON SHA-256, matched/defaulted/ignored unit counts, applied/changed edges and native formula. Exported RPLAN provenance retains the exact COI parameters; RCTX source hashes bind the JSON bytes while graph edge weights remain the original physical boundaries and populations remain Census counts. Configured export, native retries, replay, Run follow-ups and label-build jobs carry the source. Per-state job JSON can include `"coi":{"source_name":"selected-coi.json","weights_json":"{...}"}`. This is serial explicit-job execution, not automatic native State filesystem orchestration.

Source limits: 3 MiB UTF-8 JSON, 100,000 bounded unit IDs and a 200-byte source name. Duplicate keys (including escaped aliases), unsafe/oversized IDs, negative/nonfinite weights and arithmetic overflow reject the browser Run. The shared native CLI parser also rejects ambiguous or invalid factors; its existing State wrapper still warns and falls back on a COI error. Selecting or clearing a file never runs a plan. Saved original bytes are retained; Open remains inert, and input changes invalidate exports until another explicit Run. Explicit multiscale run artifacts also accept request.coi. This follows native State behavior: COI post-weights only the tract-level METIS seed, for all tract/county, BG/tract and BG/county pairs. Fine/coarse Wilson sampling and percentile edge-cut ranking remain unweighted. Block-group source IDs are ignored rather than aggregated to parents; select tract GEOIDs to affect initialization. Fixed/adaptive/build/replay/export share this boundary. The result records tract-seed-only scope and the original source hash; RPLAN retains exact inputs and RCTX keeps original physical boundaries. The main multiscale selector now accepts a local COI JSON file and offers a separate Clear control. National runs use that exact file for each selected state. Missing tract IDs default to one and out-of-state/block-group IDs are counted as ignored. Results display the source hash and matched/ignored/changed-edge counts. Original source text is retained in local projects and practitioner exports; Open remains inert. The existing replay UI also accepts explicit run artifacts.

Two shared kernel tests and four existing native CLI COI tests pass. Actual browser checks exercise selected-file replacement/Clear, visible source evidence, negative-source rejection, safe source retention and inert Save/Open. ### Shared-content workbench archives

Save workbench archive preserves the existing `bisect-workbench-archive-v1` representation whenever it fits the 128 MiB disk limit. The stored archive remains bounded at 128 MiB. Expanded string content, including repeated uses and object keys, is bounded at 256 MiB before any reference is installed. The table admits at most 2,048 strings and 10,000 references; paths are at most 64 segments. Closed fields, unique paths, existing own properties, null targets and unsigned safe integer indices are required. Prototype paths, duplicate JSON keys, unused table entries and expansion beyond the budget are rejected. The shared format contains strings and JSON paths; it does not resolve URLs, filesystem paths or executable objects. These are parser and resource guards, not source authentication or a guarantee of low device memory use.

### Explicit state batch Resume

**Resume unfinished states** continues a cancelled or interrupted batch in the same page session. A completed batch with failures can retry those failed states. Successful states retain their exact native receipts, prepared Census graph/geometry and selected follow-up outputs; their preparation and engine execution are skipped. Failed and unfinished states execute again with the original per-state inputs and seeds. Fresh native selection and congressional allocation remain authoritative, results retain selection order, and worker slots are capped to remaining work and available concurrency. Resume can itself be cancelled and continued again.

Reuse requires a live capability held privately by the scheduler, plus unchanged request/source identity, scheduled states, native selection, loaded WASM artifact and hashes of every retained row. The prior worker pool must already be closed. JSON validation rejects invalid values and accessors before copying checkpoint contents. Checkpoint callbacks receive copies, so they cannot alter the scheduler's retained native results. Input edits retire Resume; project renaming and Save preserve it. Imported/autosaved results do not carry the live capability, remain unverified and require fresh Run. No execution starts on Open, and cross-session resume still requires a separate verification design. Output installation and full native acquisition/orchestration remain unfinished.

A mixed raw-Census/prepared job verifies exact source preparation and native follow-up retention without preparing the completed state again. Existing state batch regression compares 54 complete native-host receipts, including 50 synthetic state graphs; source regression compares 12 preparations and 12 native Run/workflow receipts across three vintages and four resolutions. This synthetic coverage does not establish all-state original Census capacity.

### Compressed local workbench backups

When a workbench snapshot exceeds 128 MiB even after sharing repeated strings, Save automatically compresses the shared archive with gzip. Smaller JSON workbench archives retain their existing format. The downloaded file keeps its `.bisect-workbench` extension; Open detects the byte format. The stored file remains bounded at 128 MiB. Gzip decoding stops above 256 MiB, and shared-reference expansion independently retains its 256-MiB string budget. The existing schema, four-million-value, depth, exact-number, duplicate-key and unsafe-reference checks still apply in the archive worker. Corrupt gzip, compressed legacy schemas and expansion over either bound fail before project installation. Compression requires browser CompressionStream/DecompressionStream support.

This enables a backup to retain California's original selected TIGER/PL94 inputs alongside its prepared graph and display geometry: the actual Chrome handoff archive is about 90.5 MiB. Open remains inert; it does not execute the engine or acquire sources. The graph handoff also preserves selected demographics/COI files and election/native-export settings while applying the prepared district suggestion. `test_compressed_workbench_archive.mjs` checks lossless restoration, corrupt streams, unsafe reference paths and both expansion bounds; `test_project.mjs` checks handoff settings/source retention and existing import/cancellation guards.

The full original-source California browser gate now passes in an isolated Chrome profile with actual WASM workers and external requests blocked. Starting from the retained source workbench, it explicitly prepares Census inputs, compares graph and geometry bytes exactly with the independent/native references, hands off the graph without losing auxiliary files or electoral settings, and runs the native 52-district configuration and requested analysis/map/report workflow. The entire result matches the native host. The interactive preview renders all 9,129 tract assignments; its explicit topology profile now shares the two-million-position allowance with source-exact-large, while smaller profiles retain their limit. The result backup is about 93.9 MiB and preserves original selected sources. Reopening it performs no engine execution and keeps native workflow exports disabled until fresh execution. Analysis retains its disclosed partial status for missing optional election data; maps and report complete.

`test_full_ca_browser_zip.py` independently checks both downloaded ZIPs for CRCs, duplicate/unexpected entries, full native receipt, exact plan/context/manifest/effective YAML, assignments, workflow receipt and every workflow file. Evidence: `target/full-ca-browser-validation.log`, `target/full-ca-browser-zip-validation.log`, `target/full-ca-browser/evidence.json` and `target/full-ca-browser/california-plan.png`. The combined `-LargeStateChecks -BrowserChecks` build gate runs this full check; the direct map-model regression runs with large-state checks. ### Advisory loaded-artifact check in composed manifest replay

`verify-manifest-replay` now retains the native advisory binary check in its staged receipt. Native ILP/certificate prechecks run first. ### Correct ILP node population-tolerance contract

Per-node report review exposed a shared native dispatcher bug: run_all_splits_ilp computes the METIS multiplier1+t/node.k and passed that same number into ILP formulation/solver/LP APIs, whose argument is a relative tolerance fraction. For a10% requested final tolerance and a two-district root, the intended ILP fraction is0.05; passing1.05 effectively removes useful population balance constraints.

The observed counterexample is a4x4 grid of100-population units. Both native State dispatch and WASM branch-and-cut/iterative-separation returned1,500/100 population splits and a two-edge cut, failing the requested tolerance. After correction, both return800/800 and the balanced minimum four-edge cut. The shared tree dispatcher now supplies the relative fraction t/node.k to ILP model/solver/export and keeps1+t/node.k for the native METIS fallback. It passes those two numerical roles explicitly to an internal helper, avoiding subtraction/cancellation and preserving the existing standalone split_subgraph_ilp helper's legacy parameter interpretation.

Resume requires the original in-memory checkpoint capability and exact input/checkpoint agreement. It does not prepare sources, partition, access output paths or save files. Run re-inspects that exact master command, validates every queued recipe identity and command, applies native filters/reprocess intent and uses the requested CPU-capped worker policy (including zero automatic capacity). Print-only and policy/source mismatches stop before preparation/partition. Native States selects one vintage; the existing multi-year Run workflow remains separate.

While a master policy is attached, manual batch worker and all-years controls are disabled. The policy is shown with the queue, and an explicit detach action restores manual selection/worker controls while retaining the per-job algorithm flags. The manual worker UI keeps its existing 1–16 range; native policy requests are not reduced to that UI range and can use available selected-state CPU slots. Saved checkpoints retain the master native review and require a fresh matching review plus full native output replay before imported outputs can be reused. Live Resume preserves completed states and verifies unchanged policy/source identities. Fresh bulk batch and selected-plan output handoffs retain the native command version instead of falling back to v1.

`test_native_states_queue.mjs` compares complete synchronous Rust replies against the native host while exercising explicit handoff, original-source identity refusal, filtered CVD Runs, requested workers=100 with two available CPU slots, zero automatic capacity, cancellation/Resume, saved replay and preflight refusals. Three tiny synthetic source states are supplied; two are selected. `test_native_states_queue_browser.mjs` checks the actual inspect/apply/Run UI with real workers, disabled manual controls, exact ZIP exports, inert Open, explicit saved replay, output-version handoff and inert detach. `test_native_states_queue_zip.py` independently reads master policy metadata, source/argument/request hashes, applied CVD options, physical plan/context and native assignments. These gates run with the workbench build; browser checks require BrowserChecks. This is scoped queue-policy evidence and does not establish national original-source capacity, arbitrary host filesystem discovery, external backends or full practitioner/TUI parity.


The native `bisect run` command is now separate from the YAML/TUI configured Run tools. Its exact 20-field parser (including Stage and RunType enums) and native default-mode compositor are shared by CLI and WASM. Choose **Inspect native multi-year Run options** to review flags and defaults; year=all retains native 2020/2010/2000 order. The native entry branch currently consumes nine fields and leaves eleven parsed fields unused; the inspector names those fields, including the native print-only gap. The browser execution boundary explicitly honors print-only intent and does not reproduce the native ignored-flag execution bug.

Use the graph or full request-template tools to compile actual native Run defaults onto one eligible congressional tract graph. These tools execute only the selected state/vintage; they do not schedule the other selected years/states. Actual Run defaults can differ from States presets, so they are compiled through the shared Run factory rather than approximated with States flags. Existing native allocation, population retry, prepared-source validation and physical RPLAN/RCTX export machinery is reused. Output paths, reset and outer workers remain retained intent in this operation; no deletion, source discovery or folder access happens. Explicit Run retains original Run flags and original graph/template/auxiliary bytes in a source-hashed recipe. The ZIP includes run-flags, request bytes, native index assignments and physical plan/context. Map and native-folder handoffs retain parsed DPI and version, require explicit execution, and do not authenticate historical runs. Open retires outputs and performs no execution.

`test_native_run_command.mjs` compares 29 frozen native parser/configuration cases and 51 full native/WASM replies. The independent native oracle retains the original parser and independent Stage/RunType enum definitions plus the original native assignment body. Four graph/template executions cover edge-weighted and GeoSection on a 64-unit uniform grid and CVD on a separate 64-unit path, all with two exactly balanced districts and the native 0.5% tolerance. Default CVD fails to balance the symmetric grid within 51 native retries; that failure is retained and compared with native execution instead of relaxing tolerance or fabricating a plan. Browser tests cover explicit compile/handoff/Run, graph/template workers, inert print-only/Open, original-source ZIP and DPI/version handoffs. Independent Python checks validate source/request identities, native assignment mapping and exact plan/context bytes. All 83 native CLI argument tests, 87 single-State compilations/61 Runs, and the existing States bulk/native/browser regressions pass on the new build. Native Run multi-year acquisition/scheduling and full practitioner/TUI parity remain unproven.


The native Run tests also call the native CLI configuration and GeoSection/CVD kernels independently of the WASM adapter. Their complete population-retry sequences match for grid GeoSection, successful path CVD (accepted attempt 22, seed 22) and exhausted grid CVD (all 51 attempts fail). Metadata binding uses equals-form values and an already eligible graph code; leading-hyphen version/output strings and a filter containing both RI and a literal --help value remain data. A retained pre-correction WASM rejects the regression fixture, while the corrected compiler preserves original values. Prepared-State result tables now unwrap native Run/States/State results and expose requested/effective accepted seed, accepted attempt and the existing full retry table. None of these measurements is a global-optimality or source-authentication claim.
